recent_posts.title: How to build your first game without a programming degree
recent_posts.summary: Modern game engines like Unity, Unreal, and Godot have made game development accessible without a programming degree. Visual scripting, asset marketplaces, and drag-and-drop tools let beginners focus on design logic rather than code. A realistic beginner workflow starts with a tiny concept, builds a graybox prototype, implements core mechanics, adds feedback systems, then replaces placeholder art. Common pitfalls include scope explosion, tool-hopping, and tutorial dependency. A basic playable game can be completed in 2–3 months. The real barriers are iteration discipline, scope control, and player empathy — not technical skill.

recent_posts.title: Are Game Design Courses Expensive? A Proven Guide to Game Design Course Costs 2026
recent_posts.summary: A breakdown of game design education costs across different institution types in 2026. For-profit schools like Full Sail, Gnomon, and DigiPen can cost $40,000–$205,000+, while public universities run $10,000–$25,000 per year. Community colleges offer the most affordable entry point with transfer agreements. Hidden costs include hardware ($2,000–$3,500) and software licenses (~$600/year). Self-taught paths via free tools, YouTube, and bootcamps ($2,000–$10,000) are also viable. The key takeaway is that portfolio and dedication matter more than the prestige of the institution, and lower debt gives more career flexibility.
